story: Supermassive black holes are cosmic titans with masses ranging from hundreds of thousands to billions of times that of our Sun. Long thought to sit exclusively at the centers of galaxies, scientists have discovered they can also be ejected from galactic cores. When two galaxies merge, their central supermassive black holes spiral inward and eventually coalesce. This violent merger releases immense gravitational waves that can give the resulting black hole a massive velocity boost of up to several thousand kilometers per second. This gravitational recoil can propel the supermassive black hole completely away from the galactic center, sending it wandering into the vast expanse of intergalactic space. While most large galaxies securely anchor a supermassive black hole at their core, these runaway objects prove that some cosmic giants can be cast out to roam the universe entirely alone.
angle: Supermassive black holes can be violently kicked out of their home galaxies by gravitational waves, sending them wandering alone through intergalactic space.
